name: IntuneBrew
description: A macOS app deployment and patch management solution for Microsoft Intune. Features a web portal for app management, PowerShell script automation, and Azure Runbook integration for scheduled updates. Supports 510+ macOS applications with automated version comparison, intelligent patch management, and robust error handling with automatic retry mechanisms. Includes certificate-based and interactive authentication options.
keywords: how to update mac apps intune
author: Ugur Koc

securityCheck.aiSummary: No obfuscated code or remote code execution patterns detected. No credential theft or hardcoded secrets found. The tool uses external AI services for categorization which introduces data exfiltration risks (OpenAI). Additionally, logging issue content to stdout can leak sensitive data in CI logs. Recommend data minimization/redaction, on-prem alternatives for categorization if feasible, and tighter logging controls to mitigate exposure.

noDataExfiltration.reason: The categorize-apps.js script sends app metadata (name, description, homepage) to an external third-party service (OpenAI) for categorization. This constitutes data exfiltration of potentially sensitive internal app data to a cloud AI service. Depending on data policy, this could leak sensitive or proprietary information. Recommendation: minimize or redact data before sending, consider on-prem or self-hosted categorization, verify data handling/privacy implications, and ensure usage complies with organizational policies.
